ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the solenoid is connected to the resistor R, and the magnet is released from rest directly above the solenoid and passes downward through the solenoid. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The acceleration of the magnet just as it leaves the solenoid is less than the acceleration due to gravity

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the solenoid is connected to the resistor R, and the magnet is released from rest directly above the solenoid and passes downward through the solenoid. What is the relationship between the acceleration of the magnet just as it leaves the solenoid and the acceleration due to gravity?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The acceleration of the magnet just as it leaves the solenoid is less than the acceleration due to gravity
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a vertically placed bar magnet directly above the solenoid; the upper end of the magnet is labeled S, and the lower end is labeled N; below is a solenoid with a vertical axis, and the two ends of the solenoid are connected through the wire on the right side to the resistor R, forming a closed loop; the two points a and b are also labeled on the right side. The meaning of the problem states that the magnet is released from rest and passes downward through the solenoid. Then reason: When the magnet has just left the solenoid, the magnet is still moving downward, and the magnetic flux through the solenoid is decreasing. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current in the closed loop always obstructs the change in magnetic flux, so it will obstruct the magnet from leaving the solenoid, that is, it produces an upward magnetic resistance/attraction force on the magnet. At this time the magnet is subject to gravity mg downward, and at the same time is subject to the force of the induced magnetic field upward, so the downward resultant force is less than mg. From Newton's second law, it can be known that the downward acceleration of the magnet is less than the acceleration due to gravity g.
